name: WWE (TKO Group Holdings)
notes: Event-host shape: WWE stages premium live events plus weekly Raw/SmackDown TV; the 2026 Saudi calendar is three events (Royal Rumble 31 Jan, Night of Champions 27 Jun, Crown Jewel 7 Nov) plus WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh in 2027. No event entity exists in the schema yet, so events are recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts, not as clubs.

Saudi partnership origin: announced 1 Mar 2018 as a 10-year strategic multiplatform partnership with the Saudi General Sports Authority in support of Vision 2030, beginning with the Greatest Royal Rumble (27 Apr 2018, King Abdullah Sports City, Jeddah).

GEA expansion: on 4 Nov 2019 WWE and the Saudi General Entertainment Authority expanded their live event partnership through 2027 to include a second annual large-scale event; Riyadh Season (the GEA's annual festival, launched Oct 2019) hosts the annual Crown Jewel event.

2026 events are GEA/Riyadh Season productions: the Crown Jewel 2026 announcement (1 Sep 2026) comes 'from the General Entertainment Authority, on behalf of HE Turki Alalshikh, in partnership with WWE', and the Royal Rumble 2026 announcement (9 Dec 2025) is under the leadership of HE Turki Alalshikh with GEA and Riyadh Season.

WWE is part of TKO Group Holdings (NYSE: TKO), a controlled company: its FY2024 10-K states Endeavor subsidiaries held about 53.9% of voting interests, and after Silver Lake's take-private of Endeavor (completed 24 Mar 2025) Endeavor retains its controlling stake in TKO.
Crown Jewel 2026 is at 'Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD' - the venue name itself carries the host's brand.

name: Esports World Cup (Esports Foundation)
notes: Event-host shape: EWC is an annual tournament, not a league; the 2026 edition ran 6 Jul - 23 Aug 2026 in Paris (moved from Riyadh; officially confirmed 20 May 2026), with 25 tournaments across 24 games and a $75m prize pool. The 2027 edition returns to Riyadh. Event-host placements (host, title sponsor) have no schema yet, so the event's commercial facts are recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts and as org deals.

Organiser: the Esports Foundation (EF), formerly Esports World Cup Foundation (EWCF), a Riyadh-based non-profit announced by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on 31 Oct 2023 (event launch) and formally established September 2023; renamed Esports Foundation on 31 Mar 2026. It is funded by a sports grant from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund; the Saudi cabinet named the crown prince chair of its board of trustees on 2 Sep 2025.

Tournament operator: ESL FACEIT Group (ESL, FACEIT, DreamHack) is the Official Operating Partner of the EWC. EFG is wholly owned by Savvy Games Group, which is PIF-owned and chaired by the crown prince.

The Club Partner Program pays 40 clubs: $20m committed in 2026 (six-figure base per club, up to $1m per club), over $100m distributed across the first three years. Club participation does not guarantee a tournament spot; all clubs qualify per game.
The Club Championship pool was $30m of the $75m total; AG.AL won the 2026 Club Championship ($7m). Organizations in total took $68.6m out of EWC 2026 (The Esports Advocate, 2026-08-25).

2026 games (25 competitions, from esportsworldcup.com/en/competitions/2026): Apex Legends, Chess, CoD Black Ops, CoD Warzone, Crossfire, CS2, Dota 2, EA FC Pro, Fatal Fury: CotW, Fortnite, Free Fire, Honor of Kings, League of Legends, MLBB, MLBB Women, Overwatch, PMWC (PUBG Mobile), PUBG Battlegrounds, Rainbow Six Siege, Rocket League, Street Fighter 6, Teamfight Tactics, Tekken 8, Trackmania, Valorant.

The inaugural Esports Nations Cup was postponed from Nov 2026 to Nov 2027 (The Esports Advocate, 2026-08-18). The Olympic Esports Games are no longer tied to Saudi Arabia: the IOC and the Saudi Olympic Committee ended their 12-year deal on 30 Oct 2025.

The 6 meetings: Saudi Cup meeting (13-14 Feb 2026, King Abdulaziz Racecourse, Riyadh), Dubai World Cup meeting (28 Mar 2026, Meydan Racecourse), Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe weekend (3-4 Oct 2026, ParisLongchamp), Qatar Goodwood Festival (28 Jul - 1 Aug 2026, Goodwood), Qatar Racing British Champions Day (17 Oct 2026, Ascot), Emirates Poules d'Essai French Guineas day (10 May 2026, ParisLongchamp).

Distinguish state bodies from private royal-family vehicles: Jockey Club of Saudi Arabia, QREC, Abu Dhabi Sports Council, Visit Qatar, Emirates and the PIF projects (Qiddiya, NEOM) are state or state-fund money; QIPCO and Qatar Racing are private companies of members of Qatar's ruling family; Godolphin is the Dubai ruler's own racing operation.

name: Dakar Rally (Saudi Arabia)
notes: Event-host shape: one event, not a league of clubs, so no clubs are recorded; event facts and team/vehicle-livery sponsors are recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts. The 2027 edition runs 1-15 Jan 2027 with start and finish at King Abdullah Economic City (Rabigh) on a loop route (Arab News, 6 May 2026).

Organised by ASO (Amaury Sport Organisation) and Saudi Motorsport Company in cooperation with the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation (SAMF), under the supervision of the Ministry of Sport (Arab News, 6 May 2026; saudimotorsport.com).

Dakar has been held in Saudi Arabia since 2020 (48th edition in 2026, 3-17 Jan, Yanbu, 159 crews, 13 stages - FIA, 20 Dec 2025); 2027 is the eighth Saudi edition. Dakar director David Castera said in June 2023 the rally would stay in Saudi Arabia until at least 2029 (Motorsport.com es, 4 Jun 2023).

The 2027 route was unveiled around May 2026: about 5,320 km of timed specials, the longest Saudi-era competitive distance, with three entirely new stages (Arab News, 6 May 2026; Saudi Press Agency). Entry list not yet published; registration deadline 20 Oct 2026.

Official partners per dakar.com/en/dakar-world/partners (fetched 25 Sep 2026): host country Saudi Arabia (visitsaudi.com); institutional partners Ministry of Sport (mos.gov.sa), SAMF (samf.gov.sa), Saudi Motorsport Company (saudimotorsport.com); official partners BFGoodrich, Defender (Land Rover), Hero MotoCorp, Motul; official timekeeper TUDOR; technical partners Diverse Extreme Team and Wega; official supporter Kahoot.

Risk: as of Sep 2026 the regional security situation is worsening (Houthi attacks; the WRC's Rally Saudi Arabia planned for 12-15 Nov 2026 was cancelled and not replaced after Toyota and Hyundai travel bans). Dakar 2027 remains scheduled; re-check status before publishing.

name: Saudi-backed professional boxing (Riyadh Season, The Ring, Zuffa Boxing)
notes: Event-host shape: the entities are fight cards, not clubs, so no clubs are recorded; events are listed on the matching issue. Saudi money appears in three forms: Riyadh Season (GEA) host/title deals on cards in Riyadh and abroad, Sela's 60% ownership of Zuffa Boxing (TKO holds 40%), and Turki Alalshikh's personal ownership of The Ring magazine and its belt brand.

Zuffa Boxing is a joint venture announced 5 Mar 2025 by Turki Alalshikh, TKO Group Holdings and Sela ('A Public Investment Fund (PIF) company', per the TKO release), TKO serving as managing partner. Thomas Hauser in The Guardian (28 Jan 2026) reports Sela owns 60% and TKO 40%; the split rests on that single press report and should be checked against TKO filings.

Paramount+ is the exclusive US/Canada/Latin America home of Zuffa Boxing from January 2026 (announced 29 Sep 2025); The Guardian reports Paramount is 'believed to be paying Zuffa Boxing $100m a year' for 12 cards.

The Ring magazine (The Ring Magazine FZ-LLC, Dubai) has been owned by Turki Alalshikh since November 2024; he is chairman of the General Entertainment Authority and president of the Saudi Boxing Federation. The Ring site's own partner wall lists PIF as its 'Strategic' partner and Saudi brands (anb, Visit Saudi, Saudia, stc, SRMG, HUMAIN, Sela, AROYA) among its tiered partners.

Zuffa Boxing and its allies lobbied for the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act (House-passed 24 Mar 2026, Senate pending), which would let 'Unified Boxing Organizations' combine promotion, rankings and titles - the Guardian (Hauser, 28 Jan 2026; Zidan, 1 Aug 2025) frames this as clearing the path for a Saudi-backed takeover of boxing governance.

Event lists on Wikipedia (Zuffa Boxing, The Ring, Riyadh Season) are mostly uncited; cards were cross-checked against Ring magazine, UFC.com, ESPN and press where possible. Zuffa events after June 2026 and further Riyadh Season 2026-27 cards were not fully captured.

name: Asian Tour

The International Series pages on internationalseries.com still describe the 2026 season as co-sanctioned by LIV Golf and the Asian Tour with a pathway to LIV Golf (fetched 25 Sep 2026); they may predate the July 2026 split - flagged on the matching issue.

name: FIA World Endurance Championship
notes: 20 teams run the 35 full-season 2026 entries per the official fiawec.com grid page (fetched 2026-09-26): 10 Hypercar teams and 10 LMGT3 teams; the target brief's 35 counts cars (17 Hypercar, 18 LMGT3) from 14 manufacturers.

Hypercar entries: Alpine Endurance Team (#35/#36), Aston Martin THOR Team (#007/#009), BMW M Team WRT (#15/#20), Cadillac Hertz Team JOTA (#12/#38), Ferrari AF Corse (#50/#51), AF Corse (#83), Genesis Magma Racing (#17/#19), Peugeot TotalEnergies (#93/#94), Toyota Racing (#7/#8) - 17 cars. LMGT3: Heart of Racing (#23/#27), Team WRT (#32/#69), TF Sport (#33), Racing Team Turkey by TF (#34), Vista AF Corse (#21/#54), Proton Competition (#77/#88), Akkodis ASP (#78/#87), Garage 59 (#10/#58), Iron Lynx (#61/#79), Manthey (DK Engineering #91, The Bend #92) - 18 cars.

2026 calendar (8 rounds): Prologue Imola 14 Apr; Imola 19 Apr; TotalEnergies 6 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps 9 May; 24 Hours of Le Mans 13-14 Jun; Rolex 6 Hours of Sao Paulo 12 Jul; Lone Star Le Mans (COTA) 6 Sep; 6 Hours of Fuji 27 Sep; 6 Hours of Barcelona 18 Oct; 6 Hours of Monza 8 Nov (fiawec.com homepage and entry-list news, fetched 2026-09-25/26).

Both 2026 Gulf rounds were lost to the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz shipping risk: the Qatar 1812km was postponed from March (fiawec.com statement 1 Mar and rescheduling 13 Mar 2026) and then cancelled with Bahrain's finale, both replaced by Barcelona and Monza (Motorsport.com, 2026-07-28).

Both Gulf rounds return in 2027: Prologue Lusail 21-22 Mar, Qatar 1812km 25-27 Mar, and Bapco Energies 8 Hours of Bahrain 4-6 Nov, in a nine-round calendar that also restores Silverstone (fiawec.com 2027-calendar news, fetched 2026-09-26).

Series partners per the fiawec.com partners page (fetched 2026-09-26): Rolex, TotalEnergies, Michelin, DHL, Goodyear, CrowdStrike, Motul, Bosch; suppliers Pommery, Al Kamel, MRTC, AMP Visual TV. Goodyear is the exclusive LMGT3 tyre supplier to at least 2029 (fiawec.com news, 2026-06-11).

Car-livery placements do not fit the schema yet; car-level sponsor facts are recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts. Team title sponsors carried in team names are entered as kits with a front placement mapped from 'team title/name', mirroring the motogp research.

name: Qatar Airways Premier Padel Tour
notes: Event-host shape: the entities are the tournaments on the FIP 2026 calendar, not clubs, so no clubs or kits are recorded; the event-level facts (names, cities, dates, statuses) live on the matching issue. The official 2026 calendar release announced 26 tournaments in 18 countries; the FIP calendar lists 25 (Qatar Major marked POSTPONED).

Ownership: Premier Padel was founded by Qatar Sports Investments (QSI) together with the International Padel Federation (FIP) and the Professional Padel Association, launched in 2022; QSI acquired World Padel Tour in August 2023 to create one global tour (Premier Padel release, 13 Jun 2024, fetched). QSI is wholly owned by the Qatar Investment Authority; the exact stake in Premier Padel is not published.

Title sponsor: Qatar Airways, multi-year since 13 Jun 2024 - the tour was renamed the 'Qatar Airways Premier Padel Tour' and Qatar Airways is also Official Airline Partner; the Barcelona Finals are the 'Qatar Airways Premier Padel Finals'. Owner (QSI) and title sponsor are both Qatari state entities.

The 2026 calendar was disrupted by the Iran war: the Qatar Major (Doha) is POSTPONED with no new date on the FIP calendar; per the issue's research notes Kuwait was upgraded to a Major (26-31 Oct) and Pretoria to a P1. Gulf stops: Riyadh Season P1 (7-14 Feb, tour opener), Kuwait Major, Emaar Dubai P1 (8-15 Nov); NewGiza P2 in Egypt.

FIP official sponsors (padelfip.com homepage footer, fetched 2026-09-25): CUPRA (Official Automotive Partner), Bullpadel (Official Apparel, Racket and Ball), Mondo (Official Turf), MejorSet (Official Court), Crionet (Official Technology Supplier), LedProjects (Official Lighting Supplier). These are FIP-level partners, not tour deals.

Linked team circuit: the Hexagon World Series, created in December 2025 with the agency 54 (PIF-owned) as investor and Premier Padel as 'shareholder and major strategic partner' (FIP release, 17 Dec 2025, fetched). The 2026 Europe P2 week (14-20 Sep) was converted into a Hexagon World Series event (FIP release, 4 Feb 2026, fetched); the series launch then moved to the GENERALI Hexagon Cup Madrid, 21-24 Jan 2027 (FIP release, 12 Aug 2026, fetched).
Attendance: more than 600,000 spectators attended the 23 tournaments of 2025; the Paris Major 2026 drew a record 81,000 (+26.5%) (FIP, 14 Sep 2026, fetched).

name: AFC competitions (ACL Elite 2026/27; AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027)
notes: 32 clubs in the 2026/27 ACL Elite league stage (16 West, 16 East), the first 32-team edition, from the Wikipedia 2026-27 season article (the-afc.com hubs do not list the field). League stage 14 Sep 2026 to Feb 2027; final on 1 May 2027.

The centralised finals stage is hosted in Saudi Arabia (Jeddah 2025 and 2026); the 2026 finals used King Abdullah Sports City and Prince Abdullah Al Faisal Sports City (AFC, 2025-12-23). Saudi hosting provisionally runs through 2029 (Wikipedia lead).

AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027 runs 7 Jan to 5 Feb 2027 in eight stadiums across Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar (SAFF, 2025-01-07); the Al Khobar venue is named Aramco Stadium - the AFC's first venue-naming deal (AFC, 2026-05-06).

Top-tier Official Global Partners of the AFC: Qatar Airways, NEOM, Visit Saudi and Credit Saison. Official Global Supporters include Visa, Aramco, Midea, Kelme, TECNO, Barbican and ALBAIK (AFC announcements; Sportcal tier summary 2026-05-06).

Five of the 16 West-region clubs are Saudi Pro League sides already covered by the saudi-pro-league target (Al-Ahli, Al-Nassr, Al-Hilal, Al-Qadsiah, Al-Ittihad); Al-Ahli are two-time defending champions.

name: Women's Super League
notes: 2026/27 is the first WSL season with 14 clubs, expanded from 12: Birmingham City (WSL2 champions), Crystal Palace (runners-up) and Charlton Athletic (play-off winners) were promoted; no club was relegated in 2025/26.
Title-sponsored by Barclays since 2019/20; Sky Sports shows the league from 2025/26 under a five-year UK broadcast deal.
Run by WSL Football, a company split from the FA.

name: UFC (Ultimate Fighting Championship)
notes: Event-host shape: UFC stages about 40 events a year (numbered cards, Fight Nights); the 2026 list comes from UFC.com and the '2026 in UFC' schedule. No event entity exists in the schema yet, so events are recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts, not as clubs.

UFC is part of TKO Group Holdings (NYSE: TKO), a controlled company: its FY2024 10-K states Endeavor subsidiaries held about 53.9% of voting interests, and after Silver Lake's take-private of Endeavor (completed 24 Mar 2025) Endeavor retains its controlling stake in TKO.

Abu Dhabi: UFC and DCT Abu Dhabi (Department of Culture and Tourism - Abu Dhabi) have partnered since 2010 (formal partnership 2019), extended in October 2023 through 2028; 2026 brings UFC Fight Night 282 (25 Jul) and UFC 333 (24 Oct), both at Etihad Arena, plus Abu Dhabi Showdown Week.
Qatar: Visit Qatar hosted UFC's first Qatar event in Doha in November 2025 and announced the return, UFC Fight Night 294, for 21 Nov 2026.
Saudi Arabia: Riyadh Season (GEA) hosted UFC Fight Night in Riyadh on 1 Feb 2025; no UFC event in Saudi Arabia appears on the 2026 schedule.
Parent-company link: TKO's Zuffa Boxing promotion is a joint venture with Sela, a Public Investment Fund company, announced 5 Mar 2025 - a TKO corporate deal, separate from UFC event hosting.

name: Alfa-Bank Russian Premier League
notes: 2026-27 season ran from 24 July 2026 to 29 May 2027, with a winter break after 7 December 2026 until 26 February 2027.
Named 'Alfa-Bank Russian Premier League' for sponsorship reasons since July 2026 (title sponsor Alfa-Bank).
Russian clubs have been suspended from FIFA and UEFA competitions since February 2022 following the invasion of Ukraine.
The official premierliga.ru site is behind a Yandex anti-bot CAPTCHA, so club and sponsor facts rely on club announcements and press coverage.

name: State-hosted UCI road races (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, China, Rwanda)
country: UAE / Saudi Arabia / Oman / China / Rwanda
notes: Event-host shape: these 7 races do not fit the schema yet (no event entity, no host/title-sponsor placement), so the races are recorded here as the entity list and every commercial fact is recorded on the matching issue (Beyond-The-Jersey/data) as unsourced facts and as org deals, following the UFC, Esports World Cup and horse-racing precedents. clubs and kits arrays are empty.

The 7 races (2026): UAE Tour (UCI WorldTour, 16-22 Feb, won by Isaac del Toro), UAE Tour Women (Women's WorldTour, 5-8 Feb, won by Elisa Longo Borghini), AlUla Tour (UCI ProSeries 2.Pro, 27-31 Jan, won by Jan Christen), Tour of Oman (ProSeries, 7-11 Feb, won by Christian Scaroni), Muscat Classic (ProSeries one-day race, 6 Feb, won by Mauro Schmid), Tour of Guangxi (WorldTour season finale, 13-18 Oct), Tour du Rwanda (UCI Africa Tour 2.1, 22 Feb-1 Mar, won by Moritz Kretschy).

Separate the race owner/host (the state body) from the commercial operator: Abu Dhabi Sports Council owns the UAE Tour races with RCS Sport as organiser; the AlUla Tour site is run by ASO (c) with the Saudi Ministry of Sport and Royal Commission for AlUla as institutional partners; the Tour of Oman site is run by ASO (c) with the Omani Ministry of Culture, Sports and Youth organising; the Tour of Guangxi is organised by the People's Government of Guangxi and Wanda Group; the Tour du Rwanda is organised by the Rwanda Cycling Federation.

Muscat Classic and Tour of Oman overlap in 2026 reporting: Muscat Daily describes the 6 Feb Muscat Classic as opening the Tour of Oman programme, while Wikipedia lists it as a separate one-day race on the ProSeries calendar; the race's own site says it runs 'ahead of the Tour of Oman (7-11 February 2026)'. Both are counted here; the exact governance split is unresolved.

Not counted: the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali (21-28 Sept 2025, one-off host event, covered in claims and unsourced) and a possible 2026 Tour of Guangxi women's race, which was not verified.

Sponsorship is on race titles, presenting partnerships and leader's-jersey/stage sponsorship, not shirts; the UAE Tour's own sponsors page lists Presenting Sponsor (AD Ports Group), Jersey Sponsors, Stage Sponsors and stage partners. Host fees are not disclosed.

name: Liga Portugal Betclic (Primeira Liga)
notes: 18 clubs for 2026-27, from the Wikipedia season page (the official ligaportugal.pt site is a news hub and did not expose a club list). Season runs 7 Aug 2026 to 16 May 2027; promoted: Maritimo and Academico de Viseu; relegated: AVS and Tondela.
Title/naming sponsor Betclic since 2023-24 (previously Bwin 2021/22-2022/23); competition branded 'Liga Portugal Betclic'.

Most front-of-shirt sponsors are Portuguese betting brands (Placard, Betano, bwin, Solverde.pt, Lebull) plus Emirates at Benfica. Other placements are largely local sponsors (Hospital da Luz, Lusiadas, Super Bock, Sagres).

name: DP World Tour (Race to Dubai)
notes: The 2026 Race to Dubai season runs 27 November 2025 (BMW Australian PGA Championship) to 15 November 2026 (DP World Tour Championship, Dubai); the official schedule page lists 42 tournaments plus a U.S. Open Final Qualifying row, which is not counted (europeantour.com/dpworld-tour/schedule, fetched 25 Sep 2026).

Season-labelled '2026-27' here because the season crosses calendar years (Nov 2025 - Nov 2026), matching the site's other cross-year competitions; the tour's own pages brand the season '2026 Race to Dubai'.

The tour is named for its Title Partner DP World, whose extension to 2035 is 'the largest in the Tour's history'; DP World also titles the season-ending DP World Tour Championship and is Official Partner to a further 15 tournaments a season (tour press release, 11 Nov 2025).

The five Rolex Series events in 2026 are the Hero Dubai Desert Classic, Genesis Scottish Open, BMW PGA Championship, Abu Dhabi Championship and DP World Tour Championship (rolex/2026 page, '5 unmissable events').

Gulf events: Dubai Invitational, Hero Dubai Desert Classic, Bapco Energies Bahrain Championship, Qatar Masters, Abu Dhabi Championship and DP World Tour Championship (all UAE except Bahrain and Qatar). No Saudi events in 2026; Ras Al Khaimah is not on the schedule.

Event titles change with sponsors (Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship is now the Abu Dhabi Championship; Commercial Bank Qatar Masters is now plain Qatar Masters); two events are 'presented by' sponsors (Magical Kenya Open presented by absa; Open de Espana presented by Madrid).
Tour/competition sponsors are recorded as clubId-null deals; the events themselves are not club records.

name: LIV Golf League
notes: Owned and funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund since the 2022 launch. On 2026-04-30 PIF said the 'substantial investment required is no longer consistent' with its strategy and that it will stop funding the league at the end of the 2026 season; reported spend c. $5bn to date, c. $6bn by year-end; PIF governor and LIV chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan expected to step down (Sky Sports, 2026-04-30, https://www.skysports.com/golf/news/12176/13538273/). In August 2026 LIV announced an unnamed lead investor has signed for 2027, with players set to become majority equity holders ('LIV Golf 2.0', seasons through 2030 affirmed) (livgolf.com news, fetched 2026-09-25). Show 2026 as PIF-owned and flag the change.

13 four-player teams plus wild cards (57 players); 2026 was the first 72-hole no-cut season. 12 events played Feb-Aug 2026 (livgolf.com/schedule, fetched 2026-09-25). LIV Golf Louisiana (June 25-28) was postponed and does not appear on the finished schedule (Sky Sports 2026-04-30). The season-ending Aramco LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship (Aug 27-30, The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort) was cancelled on 2026-08-17; Indianapolis became the finale (Sky Sports, https://www.skysports.com/golf/news/12176/13574162/...). LIV says 2027 will be a 10-event schedule.

League partners (livgolf.com/partners, fetched 2026-09-25): Global Partners Aramco, HSBC ('Global Pillar Partner'), Maaden, Riyadh Air, Roshn Group, Salesforce; Premium Partner Bahri; Presenting Partner JCB; Official Suppliers Arena, Corpay, DAOU, Fever, New Era, Panini, Select Event Group, Trackman; Destination Partners Government of South Australia, Hong Kong Tourism Board, Louisiana Economic Development, Andalucia Tourism. Event names carry the sponsor: ROSHN Group LIV Golf Riyadh (Feb 4-7), MAADEN LIV Golf Virginia (May 7-10).

Team partner lists come from each team's page on livgolf.com (all fetched 2026-09-25); shirt-level placement on team apparel is not documented there, so kits carry placement 'partner' and sponsorsComplete false.

name: FIM MotoGP World Championship
notes: 11 MotoGP-class teams per the official motogp.com teams page (fetched 2026-09-25); every team name carries its title sponsor.
The official calendar lists 22 rounds for 2026; race title sponsors are shown on motogp.com/en/sponsors, not on the calendar.
The Qatar GP (Lusail) was moved from 10-12 Apr to 6-8 Nov 2026 after the Iran conflict; as of 19 Sep 2026 Dorna was still deciding whether it runs (Crash.net). No Kazakhstan round in 2026.
Sponsor placement here is mapped to the schema's front value from 'team title/name'; bike-livery placements do not fit the schema yet.
